newsitem.title: PERU: Peru siege assault interrupted chess duel.
newsitem.headline: Peru siege assault interrupted chess duel.

text.p: Peruvian congressman Luis Chang Ching will never know how his last game of chess in the Japanese ambassador's residence would have ended.

Chang was engaged in an absorbing battle of wits with Jesuit priest Juan Luis Wicht when crack Peruvian troops blasted and shot their way into the building in a bid to rescue 72 hostages from the clutches of Marxist rebels.

"We were so absorbed in ending the game, so into it, that we only realised what was going on when it was obvious that they (the troops) were coming in," Chang, a member of the ruling party, told local Panamericana television on Wednesday.

Wicht, who turned down an opportunity to leave the residence with 225 hostages in December, was well-known among the hostages as a chess aficionado and once boasted in a letter to relatives that he was unbeaten after eight games.
One hostage, two soldiers and all 14 Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) rebels died in the assault which came on the 126th day of the standoff.
